review.assessment: The change modifies `jobs/sla.py` to treat `CANCELLED` status as a terminal state for time measurement purposes, resolving the issue where cancelled jobs continued to accrue SLA time indefinitely (effectively being measured against 'now' instead of their actual end time). The diff replaces an ad-hoc check (`job.status in (st.DONE, st.FAILED)`) with a dedicated check (`st.is_terminal`), which is cleaner and correctly encompasses the `cancelled` status. This aligns with the requirement that 'the clock stops when the operator stops the job'.
